We’re constantly told that “Israel is our greatest ally.” But strip away the slogan and the facts tell a different story.

Israel has never fought alongside the U.S. in any major war. It doesn’t host U.S. military bases. It has a documented record of espionage against our country, including the infamous Jonathan Pollard case. Even more troubling, it has transferred sensitive U.S. defense technology to China — directly undermining American strategic interests.

Despite all this, the U.S. sends Israel $3.8 billion a year in guaranteed aid, blocks international accountability measures at the UN, and discourages even mild public criticism. The cost isn’t just financial — it’s diplomatic, strategic, and moral.

This isn’t about antisemitism. It’s about foreign policy. Criticizing a government — any government — should never be taboo in a democracy. But in Washington, challenging the U.S.–Israel relationship is a political death sentence, enforced by a powerful lobbying ecosystem that rewards silence and punishes dissent.

Israel offers no vital energy resources, no military partnership, and no consistent diplomatic alignment. What it provides is narrative leverage — and that leverage often comes at the expense of American sovereignty and credibility.

If any other nation acted this way, it would face sanctions — not blank checks and blind loyalty.

America deserves better. A true ally doesn’t demand loyalty without reciprocity. It doesn’t compromise your values, your independence, or your security.

It’s time to break the spell. No more sacred cows. No more unspoken rules. If we truly believe in “America First,” then every foreign relationship must be subject to scrutiny — especially the ones we’re not allowed to question.
